And with my greatest respect to my good friend, I don't -- there is nothing in the record that indicates when this man took up this post, absolutely, and we can draw no conclusions based on anything from this document, which most of us in the courtroom cannot read, or many of us, excuse me, many of us cannot read, and we have no idea when this man took the position or what it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the document says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise for interrupting my colleague for P 07341. The Prosecution should be familiar with its own document. THE PROSECUTOR: It would have been helpful Your Honour if that would have been pointed out some time ago again I don't have them committed to memory I must say.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my colleague. I have this exhibit among my documents. It doesn't have this number, though, but thank you. This significantly facilitates our task. But I wanted to say that if a report is made for the period commencing the 22nd of July up until the 25th of December, then it's quite logical that this gentleman was the coordinator during that period of time. I have run out of time, and it's obvious I haven't even received an answer to my final question, but since Mr. Bruno Stojic has been mentioned at least 20 or 30 times in the report, and in the course of the examination-in-chief there are at least two subjects that I would like to deal with briefly, although I can't proceed fast enough with the witness, but if we have 15 minutes remaining at the end of this hearing, and I don't want to take any time from my colleagues, but if we have 15 minutes remaining at the end of the hearing I would like to deal with these subjects at that point in time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The next Defence team, please. Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tomljanovich, my name is Vesna Alaburic. I'm a lawyer from Zagreb and I represent General Milivoj Petkovic. Could you please close your binder to start with, because at least at the beginning you won't need your binder to answer my questions, and the documents that we will later discuss are documents that we'll be able to look at on the screen. That will facilitate our communication, and it will be easier for you to concentrate on my questions. Thank you very much. As my learned friend Mr. Scott has said, your report was supposed to show what the -- what the structure and function of the government in the HZ HB was like or, rather, in the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna later on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Oh. I hadn't finished. Sorry. Yes, specifically the -- it was the structures and process -- the political and governmental structures and processes of HZ HB, HR HB, yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Mr. Mate Boban part of that governmental structure of HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what his role was?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander-in-chief of the armed forces. What exactly his role was with the General Staff was mentioned in one of the earlier documents. I believe he also represented Herceg-Bosna abroad as its representative, as a sort of head of -- not a head of state since it's not really a state, but like a head of state as well. He also nominates the cabinet, which is then elected by the Assembly. He has his own staff. That's all I can think of off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You said that his first role was that of the leader of the armed forces. Is that because he had some other role, some other position, or was that role as commander of the armed forces one that was assigned to him? So the question is: Did this concern some other role he had?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe it's part of his duties as president of the HZ HB and later president of the HR HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I said that as president of the HZ HB and later on of the HR HB Mr. Mate Boban was the highest ranking official in Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Highest ranking, yes. That doesn't necessarily mean most influential in all periods.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I said that during the period of time that he has been charged with -- the charges relate to, Mr. Mate Boban was the most powerful person in Herceg-Bosna? He didn't only have this top position, he actually had a significant amount of power?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He always had a significant amount of power, but I wouldn't agree that he was the most powerful person in Herceg-Bosna through this entire period as his at least de facto political power slips especially towards the end, the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Since you wouldn't agree that this statement is valid for the entire period, what period do you believe that that statement is valid for?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depends on one other thing too. Let me see here, see the precise wording you had here. Yeah. Most powerful person in Herceg-Bosna. In all periods that depends if you count people are from Herceg-Bosna but not necessarily part of the governing structures like Gojko Susak. But he was a powerful man through most of this period, or all of this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, my question only concerns Herceg-Bosna officials. I'm not asking you anything about politicians from the Republic of Croatia, about Secretary-Generals of the UN, or about any other politicians. We are only discussing Herceg-Bosna and the people who worked in the bodies of Herceg-Bosna, and that is what your report focuses on too. So if you cannot say that throughout that period of time Mr. Mate Boban was the most powerful person, tell us during which period of time he certainly was the most powerful person.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll say from the outset that's a very -- because you're asking about power, I think, in de facto political sense rather than constitutional powers, and if that's the case, it would be very hard to separate Boban's own personal power from the power he enjoyed because it was known that he enjoyed the confidence of President Tudjman and -- and Minister Susak. Although in the period of 1992 and early 1993 when he did enjoy that confidence, he was extremely powerful.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us, if Mr. Mate Boban, at least during part of that period, was the most powerful person, how is it that in your report you barely mentioned him? One has the impression that he either didn't exist or he was a totally insignificant person in Herceg-Bosna. How can you explain that? In particular, because Mr. Mate Boban died and is no longer of interest to the Prosecution. Is that perhaps one of reasons?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not why. There's a number of reasons, actually. First of all, during this period, Mate Boban was involved very heavily in negotiations abroad and in the peace process and was involved in diplomatic activity, and the diplomatic activity he was involved in falls outside of the scope of this report. The other reason why he doesn't figure prominently in this report is because as far as official decisions and decrees in the Official Gazettes or in our possession from the record of documentation, Mr. Boban is rarely present giving decisions and decrees after October 17, 1993, that directly affect the HVO HZ HB or the HZ HB in general. That's another reason. A third reason is that we have some documents which are supposed to come from his office, but the documentary record from Mr. Boban's office is rather thin, and in the absence of public official materials, there's not that much. My suspicion, though, is that the main reason he doesn't figure very prominently in all of these things is because he had the function of representing Herceg-Bosna externally, and that was his most important duty during this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: With regard to the first explanation you provided, I have another subquestion. If the president of your state spent a lot of time outside the borders of the USA, would you exclude him from an analysis of the structure of the political system of government in the USA? You could just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this question, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me if I said that since there is no explanation of the role of the president of the HZ HB, your explanation of the structure of government in the HZ HB is not complete?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I disagree with that. I wouldn't say I don't explain his role. I cite all the founding documents in which his powers are outlined. I cite all of the orders and decrees which he signed, especially 3rd of July and in the early period when he was particularly active doing so. So I wouldn't think so, although I will add that I would like to have more hard archival material from the desk of Mate Boban, who, by the way, wasn't in Mostar physically during much of this period either, when he was in Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, tell us, do you know which methodology and parameters used to analyse the way in which a certain political system operates?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can use all sorts of methodologies and parameters. Methodologies in this kind of research, it's a bit like talking about, you know, hunting and fishing. If you're going after small fish, you use a hook. If you're going after an elephant, you use a very large gun. It depends on the questions you need answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you were familiar with the methods used, you'd be able to understand my question, but the analysis of unofficial centres of power in a territorial unit, is such an analysis important to be able to define the way a given system functions within such a community?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would be in such an analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I can draw the conclusion when you say "such an analysis," this implies that you don't consider your report to be such an analysis, because you haven't even dealt with the subject of unofficial centres of power in your report.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's two --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please be brief. Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It's not necessary to go into details.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- no, excuse me. I didn't answer just no. I was going to say that's not a question I can answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I haven't got time to go into details, to expand on this subject. These were just introductory remarks that I wanted to obtain. But would you agree with my conclusion that your report is not in fact an analysis of the structure and functioning of the government in HZ HB or, rather, the HR HB, but as you have said quite explicitly in paragraph 1 of your report, it's an overview of the work of the government on the basis of the rules and decisions that were primarily published in the national Gazette and they were also found in the Croatian archives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, would I not agree with that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Since I'm defending the general who was the Chief of the Main Staff in this case, I will now focus mainly on the subject of the military structure of the HZ HB, but first of all, I have a different question I'd like to put to you. You said that you cooperated with colleagues from the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, I've been following the question that you put to the witness very carefully, and you mentioned unofficial centres of power. You asked him whether he had studied them. The answer was -- well, he didn't provide a precise answer. If you put the question to him, that means that you have certain information. Can't you add to your question, supplement your question and say if that's what I have said? "Well, why didn't you put that into your report?" We can see you're trying to show that his report isn't complete, but we aren't in the know. What are these unofficial centres of power that have just come out of the blue? We as Judges know nothing about this. Perhaps it would be good to continue with this subject.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to provide an explanation, but I don't believe it's necessary to expand on this subject, ask any questions on this subject. I believe that this report cannot be considered as an analysis of the functioning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you wish.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may just complete my sentence. It can't be considered to be an analysis of the functioning of a political system because it focuses exclusively on the level -- on the legislative level. There is a formal and legal analysis, an analysis of how a political system functions has to include a number of parameters, and this would include informal centres of powers, lobbies, et cetera. This would have to provide the basis for such analysis. Since I am also a political scientist and this is a very interesting subject for me, to expand on this subject would require a lot of time, and I don't think I can allow myself to use the little time that has been allocated to me to demonstrate that this report doesn't -- isn't an analysis of how the system functions because anyone who knows anything about political science knows that this is not the case. This is just a report that concerns general laws adopted in Herceg-Bosna. It's an overview of certain documents, but I think that as we move on we'll also shed some light on these unofficial centres of power. But with your leave, I would now like to carry on with my cross-examination, and I would like to ask the registrar to show P 09689 on the screen, page 5. It concerns the structure of the military forces. It's -- it's a chart that concerns the military forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, when we were discussing the first part of this chart, you said that you cooperated with the Prosecution when this chart was made. My question is: Did you cooperate with the Prosecution when this chart that concerns the military forces was made?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this chart concerns both the military and the HVO HZ HB and the HZ HB Presidency, but if you're asking about the part on the defence department, I was there but I wasn't the one who was the authority for the --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: This is page 1. Could we please say page 5, the armed forces chart, not political and military organisation but only armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in drawing up this chart?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only insofar to make sure the diacritic marks were correct. This chart was prepared by military analysts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You told us today that Mr. Mate Boban was the commander-in-chief of the armed forces. Can you indicate where on this chart the Supreme Commander of the armed forces is represented?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not represented on this chart.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May we conclude, then, that this chart is incomplete?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with all of these organigrammes the idea wasn't to have the complete structure but a simplified version of the structure which would be of assistance to the Judges. In the general -- in the general chart, if you look at the general chart of the HZ HB and the HR HB, there is a line going from the General Staff to Mate Boban. It's just that this is down in the armed forces proper, and he's not proper in the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, does the Supreme Command of the armed forces belong to the armed forces or not?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a question you'd have to ask a military analyst.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Does the president of a parliament belong to a parliament? Does the Prime Minister belong to the cabinet? Does the Supreme Commander of the armed forces belong to the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if response to the three questions, the first question, yes. The second question, yes. And the third question, I don't know. And I think it would depend on what you mean by "in the armed forces," which is a semantic question. He certainly is --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Does a chart representing the armed forces, if it wishes to be complete, have to include the Supreme Commander to see who is in charge? If you feel that it doesn't, just say so.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this isn't the only chart in the binder, so I don't think it's necessary to put him on this particular chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: On page 2 we have a comprehensive chart and there we have a small annex on the right side at the bottom which says "armed forces." Would it be correct to assume that what we find on page 5, a sort of blow-up of this red square.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's exactly what it is, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Than would explain why the others are not included.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, I remember when we were putting these together back in December, the idea was to have the first few charts to outline the larger scheme and then to move into more detailed organigrammes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I remind Your Honours, as I have provided all the documents I wish to put to the witness, that we will come back to the large chart a little later on. Now I would like to finish dealing with this particular chart as an independent document. So can we come back to it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What would you say, Mr. Tomljanovich, what is the Main Staff according to this chart? Would you say that the Main Staff is part of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would. In my non-expert opinion, and I'm not an expert on the military issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, as you have studied the legislation of Herceg-Bosna, on what legislation do you base this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which conclusion, that I'm not an expert on military issues? Or the conclusion that they were part of the armed forces? It's my -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, I think that based on the legislation of Herceg-Bosna you couldn't decide whether you were an expert or not, so that comment is out of place. The question referred to your conclusion that the Main Staff is part of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm asking you on what piece of legislation you base such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Off the top of my head, the Main Staff and its place is outlined in the Decree on defence and the amended decree on defence. It's mentioned in Mr. Stojic's order on the internal organisation of defence. And there should be third place that's mentioned but I can't think of it off the top of any head.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I wish to put P 00588 to the witness. It's a decree on the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, may I look at my own copies of this particular decree? No? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I would like to stick to e-court so that we are all on an equal footing. The decree on the armed forces, the consolidated text from November. 1992, the part that refers to the armed forces begins with Article 21. So could the witness be shown Article 21 to 28 inclusive. So there's command and control. You can look at the entire decree also, and you will see that nowhere is the Main Staff positioned as a part of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to skim through this document on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you take me at my word that the Main Staff is mentioned in Article 11? Could article 11 be shown to the witness, please, which says that for the performance of specific tasks, and these are listed, the Main Staff is formed within the scope of the defence department and a commander in chief of the armed forces points the leading personnel in the Main Staff. If you take me at my word that these are the only provisions where the Main Staff is mentioned, would you agree with the conclusion that the decree on the armed forces does not provide any basis to conclude that the Main Staff is part of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- if I'm taking you at your word and it's not said so -- it's not made part of the armed forces in this particular document explicitly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness now be shown the first chart from the same exhibit, the political and military structure of the HZ HB. This is P 096810, page 1 from this set of charts, and it refers to the political and military structure. We've already had it on the screen. Yes. It seems we have it now. Mr. Tomljanovich, who is at the top of this chart?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that he was president of the HZ HB and the supreme commander, could we just establish very quickly some parts of this chart, which I need for my purposes, is it beyond doubt that the HVO HZ HB is the executive branch or the cabinet?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And from 17th of October, 1992, it's also the legislative branch.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You're referring, when you said --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: -- legislative to the HVO HZ HB, while the HVO presided over by Mr. Prlic or the HVO presided over by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you make a reference to the HVO HZ HB, that's -- that's the body here in the middle of the chart presided over by Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the chart says. In your view, then, this body also had legislative functions?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had -- not only did it have legislative functions, it took over the legislative functions of the HZ HB Presidency after the 17th of October, 1992. On a temporary basis, but it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, these are two different bases, but we'll move on. Would you agree that the military police was a special organisational unit within the defence department?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, boy. The place of the military police relative to either the armed forces or the defence department gets way beyond what I'm capable of talking about as a non-military expert. It's subordinated to the military defence department, but it's -- the place of the military police in that structure is something I really can't talk about with authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But I'm only asking you to read the chart. So far you've only been reading and commenting on what was written down or drawn, so please continue doing so. According to this chart, is there a -- military police separate unit within the defence department? Yes or no? It's very simple. We're wasting too much time on simple things.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's underneath the defence department. It's underneath Mr. Coric, who is in the defence department, but in this chart the military police aren't in the box for the defence department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was the military police directly subordinated according to this chart to the assistant minister for security and also according to the documents you studied?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, directly in the second instance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Are there grounds to conclude, then, that the military police did not fall within the authority of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's grounds to think so, although I couldn't tell you if it in fact did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The Main Staff is presented here as a special organisational unit within the defence department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The Main Staff is simultaneously subordinated to the Supreme Commander of the armed forces who is the president of the HZ HB. So it is subordinated to two persons, the minister of defence and the Supreme Commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The armed forces are outside this box. They are shown as a separate unit.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I will read to you, and if you want to go back to the provisions to check whether what I've read out is correct you can do so. The armed forces are defined in Article 25 [as interpreted], paragraph 5, as follows: The armed forces are organised as command units and institutions. The armed forces are organised into commands, units, and institutions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have the original document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Based on what we've said so far, I'll offer you a few conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. What text are you quoting from? Not the decree on the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The decree on the armed forces, P 00588, Article 24, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Oh. I had understood Article 25. Sorry. That's what it -- in that case, it might be an idea to correct the transcript, because there you find Article 25 mentioned. That's what I had heard. It's a slip of the tongue perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I do see that in -- in the transcript, page 69 -- there is an error. It should say 24, not Article 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to this organisational chart, would you agree with me that the term "HVO" refers exclusively to the executive branch presided over by Mr. Jadranko Prlic?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have the chart in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we go back, please? If we can go back to P 09689, page 1.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So the concept of HVO is linked exclusively to this body of executive power. Would you agree that the armed -- that the army is calmed the armed forces of the HZ HB, not of the HVO? And would you agree with me that the Supreme Commander of the armed forces is the president of the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I explained yesterday that the HVO HZ HB is the name of the cabinet officially, but it gets called the cabinet colloquially. There are municipal governments which are also HVOs. And colloquially people do call the armed forces the HVO, but in official legislation it's call the armed forces of the HZ HB. And Mr. Boban is the Supreme Commander. Or was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we are dealing with a de jure analysis now, so we'll stick to the terminology used in the legislation. We can remove this chart now, and I will now put to you a number of questions in order to show that all communication in the direction of the armed forces did not flow exclusively through the Main Staff as could be concluded from this chart, but that, rather, this communication flow was much more complex. And this will be very important for us in these proceedings when establishing responsibility and possible omissions to prevent or punish. Could we now please look at the decree on the armed forces, P 00588. I will try to quickly go through some of the key provisions in order to define the powers of individual bodies of Herceg-Bosna in relation to the armed forces. Let's begin with Article 26, paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A question to the registrar. Would it be easier if I were to say what page it was in the English text, as my case manager has the page numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be easiest if you told us the e-court page numbers, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I -- oh, the number's down here. Article 26, 0030132. I see it's here now. If we -- yes. Yes. We can see Article 26 here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Article 26, paragraph 1, reads as follows -- oh, this is not the document. Excuse me. The Croatian text is the wrong document, but as the witness reads English -- now I see that there is an error in the translation in the English text. Article 26 reads: "The total size, structure, and composition of the armed forces shall be prescribed by the HVO, which will also prescribe the formations and the dynamics of mobilisation." May we conclude, based on this provision, that the HVO, rather than the Main Staff, decides on the structure or formations and dynamics of mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly what it says in this article.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could we now look at article 29 of this decree. In paragraph 1 it says that: "The Supreme Commander establishes the basics of the structure of the armed forces." So may we conclude that this is not something that is decided by the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a power given to the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's right. Article 9, paragraph 1 of the decree. 00300126. It reads as follows: "The defence plan of the HZ HB shall be adopted by the HVO." So may we conclude that the Main Staff does not decide on the defence plan?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it on the screen, but, yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I -- excuse me. May I come back to Articles 26 and 29? I have the feeling that between Article 26, paragraph 1, and Article 29, paragraph 1, there is a kind of an medley because both the Supreme Commander determines the basic structure, the system, but the HVO also prescribes the structure and the numbers and the dynamics, the structure or formations. Is there a clear dividing line between the competencies of the HVO on the one side and the president on the other side? And how did it work in practice, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honours, I can explain why I didn't put that question. I didn't put it because I feel that the delineations are clear, the distinctions are clear. The Supreme Commander establishes the basics of the structure, whereas the structure itself is established by the HVO. And in all the countries of the former Yugoslavia, the higher level always decided on the basics, and then the lower level would deal with the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with this explanation, Mr. Tomljanovich?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the last part, yes, although the first part it's only clear insofar as you can clearly define "basic." If you know exactly what the difference is between the basic decisions and the general decisions which follow after it, then it's clear. But from this alone, I don't know what exactly that means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Are you aware of any document which shows the decisions taken by the president on these basic structures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not, but I was deliberately not looking at military structures.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we can move on. Article 9, point 3 of the decree, it's 00300126, prescribes that the HVO determines the amount is of and the ways of safeguarding the financial means for the needs and tasks of defence. So is it the Main Staff that determines these issues?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I know from other evidence that it was -- the cabinet had to deal with the financing of the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: As for mobilisation, Article 37 of the decree, number 00300135, reads as follows: "Mobilisation of the armed forces is ordered by the president of the HZ HB." That's point one. So it's the president of the HZ HB who orders mobilisation. And let's go back to Article 9 now, the competencies of the HVO, point 6, page 00300135. The president orders, but the HVO decides on implementing mobilisation. So can we conclude that the Main Staff has no authority to decide on mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's implicit here, and I've also never seen any mobilisation orders issued by the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 20 to 6.00. It's time to have our 20-minute break now. We'll resume at 6.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Counsel Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, the sixth topic on the -- provision on the armed forces, Article 29 of the decree, it's page 10 on e-court, it is control and command, and Article 29 of that decree states that the Supreme Commander shall determine the basic structure of the armed forces and the system of control and command. We're talking about point 1 of Article 29. May we then conclude that the system of control and command is something that the Main Staff does not decide upon?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're using "control and command" as a military term of art, I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Not in the military sense but in the legal sense, as it is set out in the article, in the decree. If you cannot interpret it in the legal sense, then I'll move on to the next topic. May I then take the nodding of your head as an affirmative answer to my question?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: An affirmative answer that I could not answer the question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: May I then take it as a lack of legal knowledge that makes it impossible for you to answer the question about the contents of Article 29 of the decree, point 2 of the decree on the armed forces? Is it a lack of legal knowledge which prevents you answering my question?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say -- it might be a problem with the translation, because in the translation your question mentions control and command. In the original, it's a system of leading and commanding, a system of, and setting up the system of leading and commanding doesn't necessarily mean command and control in a military sense, from what little I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, I was very precise when I spoke about control and command, and if you interpreted legal norms then you must know the title defines the contents, and the portion of Article 29 means control and command of the armed forces. So anybody who has elementary legal literacy, there can be no doubt that this system of control and command relates to the armed forces, and that is why I can just repeat my question once we've seen the heading whether from this provision it emanates that the Supreme Commander is the person and not the Main Staff who determines the system of control and command of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the basic structure of control -- of leading and commanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We'll move on to my seventh question, still on control and command, Article 31. Once again page 10 of the decree. Article 31 states: "Control and command of the armed forces shall be carried out through -- by commanders of the armed forces in accord wants authorisations given them." And I'd like to draw your attention to the plural of the word "commander," that is to say commanders. The word is used in the plural. Now, if we link that article up to Article 24, point 5, which defines the armed forces -- Article 24. I think it's on the previous page, which makes it page 9. Let me remind you the armed forces are defined in the following manner: "The armed forces are organised in commands, units, and institutions." When those two provisions are interpreted together, and that's what you do when you interpret a provision, would it be well-founded to conclude that control and command in the armed forces is carried out by the commanders and commands, the commanders of units, and the commanders of institutions, because they are the three elements of the armed forces? Or in more simpler terms, would it be correct to say that the Chief of the Main Staff is not mentioned in Article 31 on control and command in the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not explicitly, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll move on to Article 29, also on page 10 of the decree, and it is the plan for deployment and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I intervene, counsel. I understood that the expert said from the very beginning that he didn't write a report on the -- on military issues, on the military, that it was on political structures, but that did he not focus on military issues, whereas for almost half an hour or more than half an hour you've been asking him questions of a military nature, control and command, et cetera. I'm sure there will be other experts more qualified or better placed to answer that kind of question. If you want to waste your time, you're free to do so, but I think that this type of question, which is very interesting, can be better asked of officers and military experts rather than this witness who, in fact, filed a report focusing on structures -- political structures, and he did not focus on typically military issues. So you're going into detail here. Because then we'll have to look at the rules and regulations governing the former JNA. So perhaps this isn't the right person to ask those questions. But if you wish to use your time that way, you're free to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the expertise of Mr. Tomljanovich has to do with military matters as well, includes military questions. He quoted the decree on the armed forces. He mentioned other regulations relating to the army. He defined or, rather, he attempted to define the place and role of the Main Staff and also the Supreme Commander of the armed forces. So this witness confirmed the organigrammes that were prepared by the Prosecution, and in those organigrammes, in my opinion, the position is -- positions are incorrectly depicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand it that way. I understood that on the organigrammes he was asked to define certain terms in B/C/S, but I didn't understand that he took part in compiling the organigramme. That's not what I understood. He gave his contribution as a linguist with the terms used but not the contents, the subject matter and the contents and the links and relationships between the individual boxes in the chart.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but the witness did tell us that he explicitly took part in the preparation of the first organigramme which shows the military and political structure. He said so explicitly. He said something else with respect to the organigramme of the armed forces. Can we ask him and he can perhaps confirm it? We can look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you take part in the intellectual compiling of the organigramme for the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I might be of assistance. In the report of the expert witness, I don't know the P number but it's been on our table, page 39 until page 47, we have a chapter which says "defence bodies." That's the heading of the chapter, defence bodies. And that deals with part of what we see in the organigrammes. So this expert witness, in his report, within the frameworks of this topic political and administrative organisation of the HR HZ HB, does provide a section on defence or, rather, the army. It's another matter whether he treats this at a formal level and says that this is what is derived from the rules and regulations. But as far as I can see, my colleague is showing us the regulations and reading us as they stand, as they're set out, and I think that that's something that we must do, because the witness is offering the Trial Chamber the wrong conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't want to ask this witness any military questions. This is a witness who is showing us the structure of power and authority, including military, as recorded in regulations. Now, what I as Defence counsel for the general who was the head of the Main Staff at the time, was whether this communication towards the armed forces went exclusively via the Main Staff or whether the Supreme Commander had direct authority over the armed forces and also other bodies of the HZ HB. And this will be a very important point in defining the place, role, and responsibility of each of the accused in this trial. And of course I am most interested in the position of my own client, and of course Mr. Praljak, too, who occupied the same function. So the function of the Main Staff is what I'm interested in. So with your permission, I have only legal questions. The conclusion must be that a link be established between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you're interested in that, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel kindly be asked to slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We left off with Article 31, where it says that control and command in the armed forces is exercised by the commanders of the armed forces in conformity with their authorisations, Article 31 of that decree. And my question was as follows: In that provision or article, no mention is made of the Chief of the Main Staff. Your answer to that was: "Not explicitly." Then my next -- then I put my next question, before we entered into polemics, that the plan for the use and deployment of the armed forces, and I'm referring to Article 20 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't polemics. It was an observation. I'm listening to what you're saying carefully, and I noted you used the word "polemic." It wasn't a polemic. It was just to see how we use time. It was an observation on my part.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It was not my intention to say that you entered into polemics with anybody. I just understood this discussion as an attempt to clarify certain matters. So the concept of comment is a very positive concept, and it was not my intention to say anything bad. So I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Article 29 of the decree, and at -- the topic is the plan and orders for the deployment of the armed forces. Point 2 explicitly states that the Supreme Commander shall issue the plan of utilisation of armed forces and order their use. And the logical conclusion from that is that the Main Staff is not the body that is authorised to issue orders to the armed forces. Does that emerge from this article?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not. It doesn't expressly forbid the Main Staff from making orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: May I say a few words now? And of course I do not want to take away too much time from the Defence and Ms. Alaburic but since the issue of the place of the Main Staff of the armed forces had in a number of occasions been raised by Ms. Alaburic, I would like to draw her attention to the fact that in the report which -- which we now have in our hands, on page -- I mean report by expert Tomljanovich, page 43, and on page 43 we find paragraph 106, 106, and that one speaks about, and I quote: "The place of the Main Staff of the armed forces was spelled out in article 9 of the decision on the basic principles of organisation of the defence department." And of course if there in a way six major indents, I don't want to read them all, but just to say -- let's say if we take number 4 of those paragraphs: "The Chief of the Main Staff shall be directly responsible to the president of the HZ HB for all issues relating to the Supreme Command, unit organisation, strategic and operative plans, and the use of the armed forces in time of war or peace." And then the next indent says: "The Chief of the Main Staff should exercise superior authority over the command of the HVO within the scope of general and specific powers vested in him by the president of the HZ HB." And finally, I quote the sixth incident: "The brigade commanders shall be subordinate and responsible to the president of the HZ HB as the commander-in-chief of the armed forces and to the head of the defence department and Chief of the Main Staff within the scope of the responsibilities in accordance with the powers described above." I really believe this decision in Article 9 of the decision of the basic principles are quite clear enough to give us satisfaction that we know something about the structure of the defence forces in -- in that particular instance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I thank you for intervening, because you have enabled me to explain the error in this expertise. If the regulation that you mentioned compared to the article that I'm talking about now, it is the relationship between the laws and bylaws. Now, this article that I'm trying to analyse at present would be called, according to that terminology, a law, the -- what you mentioned would be a bylaw. Now, is this decision in conformity with the provision as a higher regulation on the basis of which the decision was taken in the first place. And the second, more important point, is whether the expert has correctly quoted the contents of the decision to which he refers. In continuation of the cross-examination, we'll arrive at that decision. I wanted to look at the article first, and I will show that this is incorrect quotation of the decision to which the witness refers, the expert witness refers. So I'd like to ask you to allow me to do this, since we're paraphrasing Mr. Karnavas in saying that step-by-step we'll arrive at that decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The ninth question, if I might be allowed to continue, linked to the decree and the demarcation of the authorities that each of the bodies had, is noted in Article 30, paragraph 2, or point 2. It is page 10 on e-court. And that article states as follows: "The Supreme Commander of the armed forces may delegate certain tasks in control and command of the armed forces to the head of the defence department." You can read all the subsequent provisions. The conclusion that can be drawn from this is that tasks of control and command of the armed forces cannot be given to somebody else, delegated to somebody else. Now, my question is: By this provision, is the Supreme Commander authorised to delegate his authorisations to a representative or head of the defence department?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here explicitly that the Supreme Commander may delegate certain tasks of leading and commanding the armed forces to the head of the defence department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, appointment and relieving of duty. Article 34, page 11 on e-court. Article 34, please. It states as follows: "The commander in the armed forces shall appoint commanders of the armed forces and relieve of duty. First of all the president of the HZ HB, the commanders of brigades and high-ranking officers shall be appointed or replaced by the head of the defence department or by commanders appointed by him." According to this article or any other rules and regulations of the HZ HB, does it emerge that the Main Staff did not have any authorisation in the appointment of officers or anybody else in the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't word it like that. I would say the commanders would be appointed by the president, and commands of brigades are appointed by the defence department or by commanders appointed by him. And I don't know who that is and if that could include the Chief of Staff, but there it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. You're reading it wrong. The president of the HZ HB shall appoint high-ranking officers and the head of the defence department and the commanders that he authorises appoints the rest. I don't know what this says in English, how it's been translated in the English version, but that is what it says in the Croatian text.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was looking at the English. Let me look at the Croatian now, if I may, and answer that again. Yeah. Commanders in the armed forces are appointed by the president of the HZ HB, and then it says: "Commanders of brigades and high-ranking officers: The president --" well. No. Well, colon. "The president -- or chief of --" should I just read it into the record in Croatian? [Interpretation] Article 34: "Commanders of the armed forces shall be appointed and relieved of duty by: The president of the HZ HB. The commanders of brigades and high-ranking officers: Shall be appointed or replaced by the head of the defence department or by commanders appointed by him."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: May we then conclude commanders of the armed forces are appointed and relieved of duty by president of the HZ HB and that commanders of brigades and high ranking officers shall be appointed by the head of the defence department and by commanders that he authorises to do so. As to the other officers -- is that what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was what I said in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have a question on this. What are the commanders of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this context, I don't know if it's the chief commanders or if it's brigade commanders or any commanders. As far as I know it's not clear, but then again I'm not a military expert, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It can't logically be commanders of brigades because they come in the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Are there several commanders in the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: According to the zones.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's the zones between the top and brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry for having interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, on the basis of Article 34, does it emerge without any doubt that the Main Staff does not have the authority to appoint and relieve of duty?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if they're authorised by the president or the chief of the Department of Defence to do so. They're not explicitly given that power here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now, tell me, to the best of your knowledge when analysing the functioning of a political system, the authorisation of a body to appoint and relieve of duty, is it important with respect to the influence that body has, wields, or is it a negligible function?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's usually a very important function.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me now? [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We now come to another topic, combat materiel, Article 41 of this decree. Page 13 on e-court. It says that "HVO defence department shall take exclusively charge of supplying the armed forces with materiel (weapons and ammunition)." And equipment, food, financial means, as well as meeting sanitary, veterinary and other needs shall be carried out by the HVO defence department in cooperation with other HVO departments and other bodies and institutions. Now, my question to you is this: Are there grounds to conclude that the Main Staff does not have any authorisation in taking care and furnishing the armed forces with combat material and materiel?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're not given the authority to do so in this article. It's given to the defence department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on to another provision, the decision on ranks, conferring ranks and promoting to higher ranks, and on promoting members of the armed forces of the HZ HB. This is Prosecution Exhibit P 00295. 295. And you mention this in paragraph 38 of your report. In Article 7 of that decision, page 2 of the electronic version, reference is made on conferring rank and promotion. If we read through this brief provision, we can come to the conclusion that authority to promote and award ranks is vested in the president of the HZ HB, the head of the defence department, and unit commanders, commanders of units in the armed forces who are authorised by the head of the defence department. Can one come to the conclusion that the Main Staff has no role to play when it comes to conferring ranks and to promoting personnel?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Main Staff isn't mentioned at all in this article.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And tell us, is it important to know who has the authority to confer ranks and promote individuals to higher positions in an army? Is it important to know who has such influence and power in such a military organisation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on to the third decision on the structure of the defence department. Judge Prandler has already referred to this. I'd just like to point out something that's incorrect in paragraph 106. The expert mentioned the control of the HVO Main Staff, and in a footnote, if I have noted this correctly, he refers to Exhibit 589. It's footnote 179. Exhibit 00586 is a decision on the establishment of a branch of the Supreme Court in the territory of the HZ HB in a time of war, and an imminent threat of war, and my conclusion is that this is an error, and the footnote should have the number 00586, which is a decision on the basic principles of organisation of the defence department. Could we please have a look at that decision in its electronic form. Let's have a look at D, items 9 to 11, that concern the Main Staff. The witness has referred to this in his -- in his report. He quotes from that document. Could we focus on the penultimate passage here. And reference was made by one of the Honourable Judges to this passage too. If we have the English and Croatian version. We've already discussed this decision, because Judge Trechsel said he failed to understand this document. In the Croatian language, the title is in -- as part of the specific authorities of the president of the HZ HB, the Chief of the Main Staff is above the command of the Croatian Defence Council. This provision doesn't contain what is stated in paragraph 106 in the report, the penultimate passage. In the report it says the Chief of the Main Staff has Supreme Command over the command of the HVO within the scope of the general and specific powers vested in him by the president of the HZ HB. Mr. Tomljanovich, my question is where does this sentence appear from, the sentence which is in dispute, since it isn't contained in the decision that the Prosecution forwarded to us?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I look at my report to see what it is I'm supposed to be talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You may. As far as I'm concerned, it's paragraph 106. It's not a problem for you to look at it.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And which paragraph are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 106.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It's the penultimate passage, penultimate item.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to me this appears to be, with a minor difference in wording, what's in the translation here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the idea of a supreme power in your -- in your text, in what way is it similar to the text of the decision?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the only difference between the penultimate point in my translation and my report and what I see here on the screen, yeah, I use the abbreviation "HVO" instead of saying Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Are you sure -- I'm sorry, just on this. Are you sure it should be defence council and not armed forces of the HZ HB? Because it could also refer colloquially to the armed forces, could it is not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yeah. Yes, and I believe it does here. I hadn't thought of that, but I'm sure it does. Yes, it hadn't occurred to me that that would be -- that there'd be any question of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Tomljanovich, please, the idea of supreme authority in your report, can you find this in the original text of the decision since you know Croatian? In what way would you be justified in copying this passage where supreme authority is referred to?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't say "supreme authority" in the English original. I say "superior authority." And let me take a look at the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the Croatian version of your report, it says "supreme authority," and in the Croatian text it says as part of the specific and concrete authorities the Chief of the Main Staff shall be superior to the command of the HVO, and he shall have such authority by -- from the president. Tell me, how does this work? How can this function in principle?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I understand it, the Chief of the Main Staff gives orders to the command of the HVO and all the operative districts within the scope of the powers which he's been given by the president of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude that the translation "Supreme Command" in the Croatian text is not correct? In fact, the translation into English is not precise?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the translation in front of me, but in the original it should be "superior authority." Yeah. And it should be something like that in Croatian, but I -- I don't know what it says in the Croatian. I don't know the words.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, what I'm interested in is the last item, the last passage in item 9, which says: "Commanders of brigades shall be subordinate and responsible to the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as the commander in chief of the armed forces and to the head of the defence department and Chief of the Main Staff within the scope of their responsibilities in accordance with the powers described above." My question is: Is one justified in considering brigade commanders to be primarily subordinate and responsible to the president of the HZ HB and then only secondarily responsible to the chief -- to the head of the defence part, after which they're responsible for accountable to the Chief of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they're mentioned in that order, but at the bottom of that order it says within their scope of their responsibilities in accord wants powers described above, so that the ways in which they're responsible to the different persons should be described earlier in this same decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: How do you interpret the word -- it says brigade commanders should be subordinate and responsible to the president of the HZ HB, but for certain matters they'll also be responsible to the other two individuals mentioned. How do you interpret this?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not what's in the English. Let me take a look at Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the English text it seems to have to do with the conjunction "and" and not the link word "aj" [phoen] in Croatian, "whereas."

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me take -- uh-huh. I'm looking at this one paragraph beginning with "Zapovijednici Brigada."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Read out the sentence in B/C/S and the interpreters will interpret for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Brigade commanders shall be subordinate and responsible to the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as the commander-in-chief of the armed forces and the head of the defence department and Chief of the Main Staff within the scope of their responsibilities in accordance with the powers described above." .

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since the way in which someone reads a text can also be a matter of great significance for the interpreters, and I assume that you will believe me when I say I'm more capable of reading this and making the pauses and accents that are appropriate in the Croatian language, would you allow me to read this text?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Read the text, and if Mr. Kovacic wants to read it, we'll have a number of interpretations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The provision is as follows -- the passage is as follows: "Brigade commanders shall be subordinate and responsible to the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as the commander in chief of the armed forces and to the head of the defence department and Chief of the Main Staff within the scope of their responsibilities in accordance with the powers described above." It is obvious that this word "a," this conjunction "a," which could be "but" in English is at issue, but I don't think it's decisive for our analysis because it -- the level of responsibility is quite clear, how responsibility is divided is quite clear. Since we are short of time I'll skip the rules on military discipline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the French translation or French interpretation is concerned, I had two interpretations, two different interpretations. The first interpretation seemed to indicate that the commander of the Main Staff was responsible to the supreme commander, to the president, whereas the second interpretation indicated "and." So I had two versions in French that can be found in the transcript. There's a very simple solution. We can ask the official Translation Unit, the Tribunal's official Translation Unit to provide us with a certified translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Is that not exactly what we have in the document now? Who else would have translated this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Translation Unit has translators or revisers, specialists, and this should allow us to clear up any ambiguity. It's important to know whether the brigade commanders under three authorities, the president, the minister of defence and then the Chief of the Main Staff or is it -- does it function in a more linear way, along the same line. Perhaps a military expert could clarify this for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, I'll now summarise everything that we have said when examining the provisions. As far as the Supreme Commander of the armed forces is concerned, if the Supreme Commander acts independently to determine how the armed forces should be structured; secondly, to order how mobilisation should be carried out; thirdly, to determine the system of command and control; and fourthly, to issue orders for the use of the armed forces; fifthly, to appoint and relieve of their duties brigade commanders; six, to appoint and relieve of their duties high-ranking officers; seven, to take decisions on conferring ranks. And there are the competencies; we don't have time to go into that. But is it justified if we conclude that the Supreme Commander has an original and a direct link with the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Has a direct link with the armed forces. Well, from this, I'm not qualified to say. If you mean direct without the mediation for either -- for all of these things without the mediation of the HVO HZ HB or the mediation of the Main Staff, then I'm not sure. A link, certainly, but a direct link without the mediation of the defence department, the HVO HZ HB, or the Main Staff and out of all seven of those --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich, if he directly appoints brigade commanders, are we talking about a direct link or not? It's very simple.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if he does, yes. But you listed seven things here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes. Now I just mentioned one thing. Let's now go back to the chart, P 09689, page 1. It's the political and military structure that is concerned here, and we have just said that the supreme commander -- that there is power that links the Supreme Commander to the armed forces directly. Since this chart doesn't show a direct link of the Supreme Commander to the armed forces, would you agree with my conclusion that this chart is not precise?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because you mentioned a direct link in one respect. This is -- and once again, I didn't have -- the parts of this chart in which I was asked is just everything above the box of the defence department. I don't know what was intended by the persons who did make those decisions, the military analysts, but I'm sure they would have -- I suspect, although I'm not sure because I'd be putting words in -- I'm putting words into their mouth to some degree, but I suspect that they think in general this is the general scheme of things, and you have to keep in mind that this is a very general chart. With something this size you can't list every single duty and every single possible responsibility on something -- on an 8.5 by 11 size.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 4D 00143. Defence Exhibit 4D 00143. We have the same chart here. If we could perhaps rotate it a bit. This is the same chart. I worked on it a bit in accordance with the legislation of Herceg-Bosna. Mr. Tomljanovich, you will see there is a line that demonstrates a direct link between the supreme commander of the armed forces with armed forces, and this would mean that according to this chart the commander of the armed forces partially communicates with the armed forces through the Main Staff and partially he communicates with them on an independent basis. Does such a chart tally with the legislation of Herceg-Bosna that we have examined today?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's certainly plausible, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I thank you. If we can move on, because I only have seven minutes left. I have only seven minutes left and there are a number of other issues I would like to deal with. As far as the relation between the HVO HZ HB, or, rather, the government, and I can remind you that you have seen in the legislation that the government would adopt a defence plan, they would determine a manner of security and the funds that had to be obtained to finance tasks and defence. Thirdly, they would determine the size, structure, and number of the armed forces. Four, they would determine establishment and mobilisation. Five, they would decide on mobilisation. I don't want to go into the details of how everything actually functioned in practice. I'd just like to focus on the legal analysis of this matter. Would it be correct to say that one can link the HVO with the armed forces? Could we have a direct line that represents such a link as shown in this chart?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although I'm not very qualified to say what's in the lower right-hand corner, I would think so, that you could make a direct line. But once again I'm not qualified to say if it's a direct line or if it's a line that goes through the defence department. And it would depend what the line was representing as well. You've listed a lot of powers here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: As far as the defence department is concerned, and I'm emphasising the fact that this is a formal analysis, it's not an analysis of how things functioned in practice, if the head of the defence department, according to the rules and regulations, can take over duties from the Supreme Commander, can take over the duties of commanding and controlling the armed forces, and if he appoints and relieves of their duties non-commissioned officers within the armed forces, if he provides the armed forces with combat material and other materiel, if he has the authority to confer ranks and to promote personnel, if brigade commanders are under his authority, would it also be justified for one to establish a direct link between the defence department to the armed forces, a link that bypasses the Main Staff? And does this chart tally with the laws and rules and regulations of the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand it as a non-military expert, that makes good sense to me. However, as a non-military expert there may be something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We could perhaps now conclude with this part. I have another three minutes left. Since military matters in this report have been discussed far less than civilian matters, I have agreed with my colleagues that I will conclude today, although there are some areas I won't be able to cover. Sir, could you please explain something for us? Could you explain the relations between the local authorities and the armed forces and tell us, according to what you managed to investigates, were politicians, local politicians or perhaps other individuals who had influence or power, did such individuals have any influence on the armed forces and on the way the units of the armed forces acted in their territory?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, military-civilian interchange at the local level is something I did not focus on. However, I do know that in some instances, particularly in the earlier period, things did happen, that political leaders did have influence over local military.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 181, you dealt with the subject of municipalities, and among other things, you referred to document P 00128, and I quote: "Municipalities acted as if they were states. They had established a means of obtaining funds and financing defence," et cetera, et cetera. My question concerns funding defence in municipalities or by municipalities. Can you tell us whether members of the armed forces were paid by the funds that municipal -- that municipalities had at their disposal or was that not the case?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is actually an issue which comes up in some of the documents that I cite. I believe originally it was the practice that the municipalities would pay them. I know that very soon on, and I'm not sure exactly when, it was supposed to be the central authorities who would be paying military personnel and that in late 1993 this was a problem, that the central HVO HZ HB, or it may have even been the cabinet by that point, wanted local governments to stop paying money to their own -- to the military in their municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'd like to remind everyone of a Prosecution document, P 05799. These are the minutes from an extra ordinary session of the HZ HB government, dated the 9th of October, 1993, attended by Mr. Praljak and Petkovic. Among other things, they mention the problem of a lack of a single means of funding. So members of the armed forces didn't have the same material position, and this means that in October 1993, as early as that date, individual members of the armed forces were financed by municipalities. My concluding question, Mr. Tomljanovich, is as follows: According to your experience when analysing political systems, does someone who pays an individual have the power to influence the way in which that individual acts?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, leaving aside everything about the meeting, just the question about someone paying an individual, generally speaking, yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes. You wanted to mention some numbers of documents that are to be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'll do that on Monday. I just wanted to ask you if I could be granted an additional half an hour on Monday or on any other day once my colleagues have concluded their cross-examination, because I believe that the questions put to the witness at the end concern my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If your colleagues agree to give you half an hour, that is no problem. All I'm saying is that it is absolutely necessary for us to conclude on Monday at 7.00, unless two extra hours are granted for another day.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm making such a request because some questions have been put that might be damaging for my client, and I would like to clarify these issues with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll see about that. I must inform you of something concerning the admission of documents. It's a document that concerns Witness BK. On the 29th of August, in order to decide to admit P 08436, we asked the Prosecution to provide us with an additional document. The Prosecution, on the 6th of September, provided this additional document, P 09696, which is an excerpt from the registry of the municipality of Prozor. It concerns a list of 162 individuals who were allegedly killed or went missing. In this list, number 51 contains (redacted). We said that the document P 08436 was a sealed document and had been marked for identification. As that is what we said, if the Defence has any comments to make, you can do this on Monday. This is the document that comes from the Prozor municipality. You're familiar with it because the Prosecution filed its motion on the 5th of September, 2006. I apologise to the interpreters because we are running a little late. Mr. Kovacic, is there anything you would like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to know whether it would be all right to respond orally on Monday. I've prepared myself to make a written response, but I don't think it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. You can work on this oral response tomorrow. I'd like to thank everyone, and I'll see you all next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
